title: Proxyless cutover and telemetry preservation play
summary: Playbook for an incremental 'proxyless' runtime + control plane cutover in private deployments (VPC/on-prem). Focus is on preserving telemetry and observability while removing in-path proxies/sidecars, ensuring API compatibility, and providing reversible Terraform patterns and safe rollback steps.
content:
Purpose and scope:
This document describes an operational play for performing an incremental cutover that removes the proxy/sidecar layer ("proxyless") from the datapath in Private Deployments while preserving telemetry (traces, metrics, logs), ensuring API compatibility with older clients, and keeping rollback deterministic.

This is intended for on-prem and VPC customers where proxies were introduced for routing, canarying, or policy enforcement and the goal is to move to a lighter-weight, direct runtime path for lower tail latency and reduced failure modes.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Target clusters run runtime v4.x and control plane v3.8+.
- Networking teams can update LB/NAT rules and perform host-level routing changes during the window.
- There is an existing sidecar/proxy that performs (a) ingress/egress routing, (b) telemetry enrichment (headers), and (c) TLS termination.
- Customer permits maintenance windows for brief restarts of control plane agents.

Goals:
- Remove sidecar from in-path for inference traffic with zero data loss.
- Preserve span continuity (trace ids) and metrics labels previously injected by the proxy.
- Maintain API contract (request/response headers and error semantics) for older client versions for at least two weeks post-cutover via compatibility shims.
- Provide a reversible and well-tested rollback path that can be executed by SREs without code changes.

High-level strategy:
1) Introduce an API shim plugin in the runtime that can emulate proxy-added headers and enrich telemetry when the proxy is absent. Ship as a feature-flagged minor runtime release.
2) Deploy shim in parallel to the proxy (side-by-side), enable observability comparison mode (dual-writing traces/metrics), run for 48–72 hours.
3) Switch routing for 5% of production traffic to the proxyless path (canary) with automated SLO gating.
4) Gradually increase traffic to 25%/50%/100% with telemetry drift checks and smoke test gating.
5) Decommission proxy once parity and stability are confirmed.

Pre-cutover checklist (operational):
- Backup: control-plane DB snapshot, runtime KV cache dump, and proxy config export.
- Confirm rollback runbook is staged and tested in staging.
- Confirm Terraform state is locked and a plan for re-applying TF to re-create the proxy path exists.
- Coordinate maintenance window with customer partners and networking.
- Create a short-lived feature flag in the control plane that toggles shim behavior.
- Validate observability export endpoints (Jaeger/OTLP, Prometheus relays, log sinks).

Terraform and IaC notes (practical tips):
- Avoid destructive replacement of network resources. Use a phased approach: add new listeners/route objects for proxyless path, don't delete proxy resources until final-phase.
- Example module pattern (text excerpt):
  module "proxyless_listener" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules//networking/proxyless-listener?ref=stable"
    cluster_id = var.cluster_id
    enable_tls = var.enable_tls
    advertise_ports = [8080, 8081]
  }
- Keep proxy resources in place but set a boolean flag proxy.enabled = false in the runtime config when shifting traffic (this allows TF to show no diffs for deletions until manual prune).
- When making TF changes, run: terraform plan -var-file=canary.tfvars > plan.txt and share plan.txt with SRE + networking for sign-off.
- For on-prem appliance bundles, create an upgrade artifact that contains both proxy and proxyless runtime bits; use a post-install hook to flip the flag.

Telemetry preservation tactics:
- Trace continuity: the shim must accept existing X-Trace-Id/X-Span-Id headers and inject them into runtime spans when present. If header absent, the shim should generate a trace id and mark origin as "shim-generated".
- Metrics labels: if the proxy previously injected labels (customer_id, route_id, model_variant), the shim must accept the same labels via runtime config overrides or read them from request metadata.
- Dual-write mode: while running side-by-side, write spans/metrics to both the proxy pipeline and the new shim pipeline so we can compare distribution and cardinality.
- Drift detection: run an automated job that computes the 95/99 latency and per-label cardinality delta between proxy and shim streams. Fail the rollout if >10% increase in 99th latency or >15% label cardinality loss for any top-10 labels.

API compatibility and graceful degradation:
- API shim behaviors to emulate: deprecated header mappings, legacy error codes (X-Err-Code), empty-body short-circuits returned by proxy for quota hits.
- Backwards compatibility layer: implement a header normalization module that maps old header names to new ones. Expose a config endpoint /admin/compat-mapping (locked to admin network) to update mappings without restart.
- Time-based compatibility flag: keep compat mode on for a minimum of 14 days post-100% cutover, then remove after internal sign-off.

Canary and gating plan:
- Phase 0: Staging: run full end-to-end (E2E) tests with traffic replay, validate traces and metrics.
- Phase 1: 5% canary for low-traffic customer segment, 6 hours. Gate: no increase in error rate over baseline (p50/p95/p99 within thresholds), no unexplained 500s.
- Phase 2: 25% for 24 hours. Gate: telemetry parity checks, no label loss, and error budget impact under 1%.
- Phase 3: 50% for 24 hours with synthetic load injections. Gate: tail-latency stable, KV cache hit-ratio within 2% of baseline.
- Phase 4: 100% for 72 hours. Gate: manual QA + SRE sign-off.

Smoke tests (examples):
- Simple generation request for known sentinel prompts, verify response checksum match to pre-cutover baseline.
- Streaming session start/stop, verify chunk ordering and no head-of-line blocking.
- Embedding query for 100 sample items, validate dimensionality and sample differences within tolerance.
- Chaos test: remove a single runtime instance from pool and validate graceful client retries.

Rollback plan (detailed reversible steps):
- Trigger condition: doubled error rate, >20% increase in p99 latency, or missing telemetry label cardinality exceeding thresholds.
- Immediate: flip the routing to send 100% traffic back to proxy path via Terraform toggle (proxy.enabled = true) or networking change.
- If TF toggle fails, use routing override in the control plane (admin API) to route to static proxy endpoint set.
- Post-rollback: gather traces/metrics for forensics, compare with pre-cutover snapshot, and create an incident doc.
- If rollback still fails to restore services, execute emergency fallback: re-deploy previous runtime artifact (runtime:v3.x with proxy hooks) via appliance restore or node agent.

Post-decommission cleanup checklist:
- Retain proxy configs in TF as an archival resource for 90 days (do not delete immediately).
- Run an observability sweep: confirm no spans or metrics with tag origin=proxy for the last 30 days (or archive them).
- Remove compat mappings after 14 days and update admin changelog.
- Run a small perf job to validate cost-savings and update Optimize recommendations for the customer.

Operational runbook (short commands and checks):
- Check active listeners: curl -sS http://controlplane.internal/admin/listeners | jq
- Enable shim feature flag: POST /admin/flags {"proxyless_shim": "on", "dual_write": true}
- Create canary TF varfile: echo 'canary_traffic_pct = 5' > canary.tfvars
- Apply routing change (dry run first): terraform plan -var-file=canary.tfvars && terraform apply -var-file=canary.tfvars

Telemetry verification script snippet (conceptual):
- Use our internal replay job: scripts/replay_compare.py --from=2026-01-01 --to=2026-01-02 --streams=proxy,shim --checks=latency,label-cardinality

Postmortem and metrics to capture during and after cutover:
- 1m/5m/1h error rate, by endpoint and customer_id
- p50/p95/p99 latency for RPC and tokenization paths
- KV cache hit ratio and miss latency
- Trace sampling rate and top entry-span latency
- Label cardinality for customer_id/route/model_variant

Open engineering items to resolve before finalization:
- Add admin endpoint to mutate compat-mapping without restart (ENG-4321).
- Make TF module output the planned network diff as a machine-readable artifact for SRE signoff (ENG-4330).
- Create a UI toggle for rollback with RBAC (Console ticket: CON-221).

Notes and rationale (why proxyless):
- Sidecar had been a useful isolation and policy boundary but added ~6–12ms median tail overhead and a brittle failure surface (proxy memory leaks).
- Proxyless path reduces hop-count and simplifies TLS termination architecture for private clouds where we control certificates via KMS integration.

Appendix A — quick checklist for on-call:
- If you see a spike in 500s immediately after routing flip: switch traffic back to proxy and collect heap profiles for proxy instances.
- If traces are missing trace ids: enable shim's backwards header acceptance and re-run a short dual-write window.

Appendix B — sample incident message for customers:
- Subject: Short maintenance — inference latency regression detected and mitigated
- Body: We detected a latency regression during a phased cutover and temporarily reverted to the previous routing while we investigate. No customer data was lost. We will follow with a postmortem and an ETA for re-try.

Owner and escalation:
- Playbook owner: Asha Patel (eng-private-deployments)
- Primary escalation: Diego Morales (SRE lead) -> Priya Shah (Network lead) -> VP Eng if unresolved in 4 hours.

End of document.
